description: The firm's stated risk appetite for the AML/CFT and AI estate, expressed as positions that are enforced in code and measured by key risk indicators. Step 2 of the GRC framework. Every position names the control that enforces it and the KRI that measures it, so appetite is a live constraint rather than a paragraph. The human view is docs/governance/risk-appetite-statement-2026.md.
review_cadence: Annually, and on any material change to the methodology, the estate or the regulatory perimeter.

approval.note: Appetite is a board act. Until R7 is minuted this document states the appetite the estate ALREADY enforces in code — it does not invent a new one. Nothing here grants tolerance the controls do not already give.

scale.name: DPMS customer risk score (0-30)

bands.meaning: Customer due diligence — within appetite on the numeric score alone

scale.hard_rules: A prohibit-flagged answer forces PROHIBITED regardless of score; any EDD trigger forces EDD regardless of score. The analyst override is a one-way ratchet: it may only RAISE the required diligence, requires a written justification, and never applies to a prohibited relationship.

appetite.statement: No dealing with a designated party, and no silent clear. A confirmed match stops the relationship and starts the TFS procedure; a screening run that cannot load a core list must read DEGRADED rather than pass.
appetite.escalation_sla: Same business day to the MLRO; a confirmed designated-party match goes to the Board immediately and starts the TFS procedure.

appetite.statement: Risk is accepted by band, not by exception: CDD to 19, SDD to 22, EDD above. A prohibited outcome is never onboarded, and diligence may only ever be raised — never lowered — by a human, and only with a written reason.
appetite.escalation_sla: Five business days to the MLRO; a prohibited outcome onboarded escalates immediately.

appetite.statement: No AI system decides, files, freezes or records. Models classify, draft and advise; humans decide. No model call may declare tools, and no generative prose may enter a filed report.
appetite.escalation_sla: Same business day to the MLRO. A model call that declares tools, or generative prose in a filed report, is an incident under the AI incident runbook, not a KRI breach to be logged.

appetite.statement: No personal data reaches a processor without an executed DPA and a confirmed transfer basis. Where the basis is unconfirmed the path is gated OFF, not merely documented as a risk.
appetite.escalation_sla: Same business day to the MLRO and the DPO; the affected path is gated OFF before the escalation, not after it.

appetite.statement: No instruction set reaches production unreviewed, and no agent holds an action that is not registered with a credential and a kill switch.
appetite.escalation_sla: Same business day to the maintainer and the MLRO; unreviewed instruction-set drift is reverted first and discussed second.

appetite.statement: Degradation is tolerated; silent degradation is not. A failed source, a dead run or a stale list is acceptable for as long as it is visible, alarmed and attributed — never absorbed into a clean-looking result.
appetite.escalation_sla: Ten business days to the maintainer for a single breach; a sustained anomaly auto-escalates to a GitHub issue on the run that detects it.

appetite.statement: No secret in git history, no known-vulnerable dependency without a recorded justification, no unreviewed third-party action in a workflow.
appetite.escalation_sla: Same business day to the maintainer; a secret in git history escalates to the repo owner immediately and triggers the history-scrub runbook.

appetite.statement: Findings are accepted as a normal output of assurance; carrying them is not. Every finding gets a root cause, a corrective action and a verification, and CRITICAL/HIGH findings carry a regression test.
appetite.escalation_sla: Reported at the next quarterly management review; a CRITICAL or HIGH finding open past its verification escalates to the MLRO within five business days.

residual_ceiling_basis: A ceiling is the highest RESIDUAL score (likelihood x impact, 1-25) the firm will carry in that domain without a treatment plan that has an owner and a date. It is the number that makes docs/policies/risk-assessment-methodology.md section 3 enforceable: 'residual risk is compared against the appetite; anything above appetite requires a treatment plan with an owner and a date' could not be evaluated while no position stated one. Ceilings are set on the methodology's own published bands (Low 1-6, Medium 7-12, High 13-25), not chosen per risk: ZERO = 6, so nothing above the Low band is carried untreated; LOW = 9, findings are a normal output of assurance and may sit into the lower Medium band while closure holds; BANDED = 12 and MEASURED = 12, the top of Medium, because both positions accept risk up to a stated boundary rather than minimising it. A ceiling is NOT a prohibition and a breach is NOT a failure: it is the trigger that requires a dated treatment. Scored by residualAboveAppetite in scripts/grc-metrics.mjs against docs/aims/ai-risk-register.md; the ceilings themselves are appetite, so only the Board may move them (resolution R7).
risk_coverage_note: Every risk in docs/aims/ai-risk-register.md is claimed by exactly one appetite position, and every position lists the risks it owns. test/grc-metrics.test.mjs fails on a risk claimed twice or by nobody, so a new register row cannot be scored against an appetite that does not exist, and an appetite position cannot quietly stop covering a risk.
advisor_zero_tolerance: CAHRA refinery inputs without OECD docs
High-risk customer EDD reviews overdue >30 days
advisor_zero_tolerance_note: Mirrored from ZERO_TOLERANCE in netlify/functions/brain-soul.js — the appetite thresholds the Advisor is told to treat as blocking. test/grc-metrics.test.mjs fails if the two lists diverge (in both directions), so the stated appetite and the appetite the Advisor applies cannot drift apart.

kris.label: Control effectiveness
kris.rationale: Every control in the assurance matrix must still point at a proof artefact that exists. Anything less means a claimed control is unevidenced.

kris.label: Regulatory obligations without an owner
kris.rationale: An obligation nobody owns is the failure mode behind 'weak ownership of key controls'.

kris.label: Model tool-calling declarations
kris.rationale: The moment a model call declares tools, the model can reach a connector directly and RA-03 no longer holds.

kris.label: Vendor assessment coverage
kris.rationale: A processor whose safeguard is unconfirmed is a transfer the firm cannot evidence a basis for.

kris.label: Unapproved prompt or agent-capability drift
kris.rationale: Sums prompt fingerprint mismatches and agent-register mismatches: either means production behaviour changed without a recorded decision.

kris.label: Obligations with no change-detection source
kris.rationale: An obligation with no watched source changes without anyone noticing. One is tolerated (ISO/IEC 42001, a standards-body publication rather than a supervisor feed); a second means a real blind spot.

kris.label: Suppressed vulnerabilities without a recorded justification
kris.rationale: Suppression is acceptable; silent suppression is not. Every entry in ci/osv-scanner.toml must carry a reason.

kris.label: Audit finding closure
kris.rationale: Findings may be open; a backlog of them may not.

kris.label: Overdue issue rate
kris.not_instrumented_reason: The register's governance rows carry an owner and a closing condition but no target date, so the KRI cannot be aged against a deadline. Instrumenting it means the board setting target dates on those rows (item 17) — recorded as the reason the metric reports null rather than zero. The engineering rows opened by the August 2026 audit carry maintainer-set dates and are counted per row by openActionsWithoutTargetDate.
kris.rationale: Kept in the register unmeasured rather than dropped: an appetite you cannot measure is a gap to state, not a line to delete.

kris.label: Risks carried above their appetite ceiling
kris.rationale: The methodology requires a dated treatment plan for anything above appetite, and until every position stated a numeric residual_ceiling that rule could not be evaluated at all. This scores every row of docs/aims/ai-risk-register.md against the ceiling of the position that claims it. A non-zero value is not a failure — it is the register saying, in a number, which risks the firm is knowingly carrying above the line it drew. It is filed under RA-08 because carrying a risk above appetite is a remediation obligation: the treatment plan, its owner and its date are what close it.
